reason: The cited evidence shows Inconel 718 performs well as a transition layer on H13 steel, but the hypothesis targets a Ni-based superalloy substrate with hot-cracking issues, not steel. No evidence is provided for the claimed thermal expansion matching, stress buffering, or hot-cracking mitigation on a Ni-based superalloy, leaving key premises unsupported.
premises: Inconel 718 provides excellent thermal expansion matching and stress resistance as a transition layer on a steel substrate.
A laser-clad Inconel 718 transition layer creates a robust metallurgical bond and alleviates stress concentration.
The graded microstructure buffers thermal expansion mismatches and reduces residual tensile stresses that cause hot cracking.
The intervention mitigates hot cracking in Ni-based superalloys that are prone to hot cracking during fusion welding.
